# a12s

> a12s runs AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex) as durable, isolated "agent computers" in Docker. A project
> declares them in fleet.yaml or creates them from code, `a12s up` runs the Fleet, and apps send them work
> (Messages) and follow their Turns and events through the TypeScript SDK (`@coltonkirsten/a12s` on npm), the Python
> SDK (`a12s` on PyPI), a browser gateway, or an HTTP API.

This file is for coding agents building ON a12s, and it is meant to be enough on its own: every command, field,
method and file layout below is exact, so copy them rather than guessing. Current release: v0.5.0 (CLI, images,
svckit, npm and PyPI packages all share the version). You never edit or vendor a12s itself: a project changes only
its own fleet.yaml, presets, images, Services and app code.

## Words

- Fleet: what one project runs. fleet.yaml declares it (metadata.name is the Fleet's name); the SDK and the HTTP API
  change it while it runs. Its version goes up by one with every change.
- agent computer (`AgentComputer` in code): one agent (harness + home drive + session + inbox). Survives sleep and
  restarts.
- Message: work in an agent computer's inbox. `send` puts one there; it is delivered at the agent computer's next
  idle moment, batched with anything else pending. Works while it is busy or asleep. `send(...).wait()` (CLI:
  `a12s send <c> "…" --wait`) returns the Turn that delivered it, once that Turn ends. Two Messages sent back to back
  to an idle agent computer usually run as two Turns (the first starts at once, the second waits for the next idle
  moment), so count results across Turns, never expect them in one.
- Turn: one run of the agent that delivers every pending Message; ends completed | failed | interrupted.
- Session: the agent's conversation. Turns continue it; a Message with fresh=true starts a new one.
- Event: journal entry, {v, agentComputer, session, turn, seq, ts, type, data} (`computer` is agentComputer under its
  old name). Types and data: turn.started {inbox: {messages: [{id, sender, via, …}]}, …}, turn.dispatched,
  text.delta {text}, tool.started {id, name, input}, tool.finished {id, name, isError, output},
  turn.finished {status, usage, tokens?: {input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite}, error?}, egress.denied {host, port,
  reason}, diagnostic {message}, permission, session.changed {from, to}, resume.failed, lifecycle {phase},
  harness.restarted, inbox.discarded. On the fleet-wide stream only: fleet.changed {version, by, names},
  agent_computer.phase {phase, error?, waiting?}, inbox.changed (the inbox summary: {pending, claimed, held, holdReason?,
  usage, …}; a burst of changes is one event) and service.phase {service, phase, health?, restarts, error?, waiting?} (no
  agentComputer). SDK-made: gap (events lost; resync). `tokens` is the same for every harness
  (input excludes cached input); `usage` is the harness's own.
- via: who really sent a Message: local (owner CLI/SDK), token:<name>, service:<name>, computer:<name>. sender is
  only the sender's own label. Trust via, not sender.
- grants.send: agent computers this agent computer (or Service) may send to. On an agent computer it adds the MCP
  tool `mcp__a12s__send` (args: computer, body; optional fresh boolean, expires seconds, replaceKey string) that
  returns a receipt, never an answer. Grants are one-way: for a reply, the other side needs its own grant back.
- Service: a non-agent container in the same Fleet (a clock, a webhook bridge, an MCP server). No harness, no inbox.
- phase (exact strings, capitalized): Provisioning, Starting, Ready, Busy, Stopping, Asleep, Error; a Service can also
  be Unhealthy. `status.phase` in the SDKs, `.phase` of each `a12s status --json` entry, agent_computer.phase events.
  One waiting for a credential with no value yet stays Provisioning with `waiting: {credentials, fix}`.

## Setup (once per machine)

Needs Docker running (Docker Desktop on macOS) and, for the token, the Claude Code CLI
(`npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code`).

```sh
brew install coltonkirsten/tap/a12s   # macOS/Linux; `a12s version` prints the release
claude setup-token                    # browser sign-in, prints a long-lived sk-ant-oat01-… token
```

Credential for `anthropic`, either: a `claude setup-token` token (recommended; Claude subscription) or an Anthropic
API key (`sk-ant-api…`). Not a copy of your interactive Claude login. Codex: `openai` = an OpenAI API key.
- `a12s creds set <name>` reads ONE line when typed or pasted (not echoed), or all of stdin when piped. The setup
  token is printed wrapped over two or more terminal lines: pasting it interactively stores only the first piece and
  the Turn fails to authenticate. Join it first, e.g. `pbpaste | tr -d ' \n' | a12s creds set anthropic`, or
  `printf %s "$TOKEN" | a12s creds set anthropic`.
- `creds set anthropic` refuses a value that isn't one unbroken sk-ant-oat01-… or sk-ant-api03-… string of about 108
  characters (spaces or line breaks inside, a cut-off paste, another secret) and prints the fix; `--no-check` skips it.
- Run it in the Fleet's directory: it stores the value at ~/.a12s/<fleet>/<name> (0600) and binds it in
  a12s.bindings.yaml (created if missing). If the Fleet's Controller is running it also sets the value there, and
  agent computers using it get it at once; otherwise `a12s up` sends it.
- `a12s up` sends every credential bound in a12s.bindings.yaml, so agent computers created from code can name any of
  them. From code: `fleet.credentials.set(name, value)`. Order doesn't matter: what names a credential with no value
  yet is created with a warning and waits in Provisioning (`waiting` in its status), then starts once it is set.
- The Controller stores credential values in its state volume (credentials.json, 0600), so they survive a restart
  of Docker or the Controller; `a12s down` removes them. No API call returns a value.
  `a12s up --memory-only-credentials` (when it starts a new Controller) keeps them in memory only.
- A bad or expired credential fails the Turn: turn.finished status failed, error "Failed to authenticate: …".

## New project

```sh
a12s init myproj && cd myproj         # fleet.yaml (defaults + one agent computer "assistant"), fleet.lock, bindings, .gitignore
a12s creds set anthropic              # see Setup for pasting the token
a12s up                               # creates the agent computers, returns when they are Ready
a12s send assistant "Reply with the single word pong." --wait
```

`creds set` runs in the Fleet's directory (after `a12s init dir`, cd into dir first). Before or after `a12s up` both
work: an agent computer whose credential has no value yet waits (up prints the warning and the fix) and starts once
`creds set` gives it one.
`a12s init` writes `harness: { kind: claude-code, version: 2.1.280 }` with no model key (the harness's default
model): add `model: haiku` to that line yourself.

`a12s init` is optional: a hand-written fleet.yaml works; `a12s up` writes fleet.lock and `creds set` writes the
bindings file. Commit fleet.yaml, fleet.lock and presets; never commit a12s.bindings.yaml. A Message sent right
after `a12s up` is delivered as soon as the agent computer is Ready. `a12s init` puts harness, image and credentials
in `defaults:`, so an agent computer created from code needs only a name and instructions.

## fleet.yaml

```yaml
apiVersion: a12s.ai/v1alpha1
kind: Fleet
metadata: { name: team }              # DNS label; also names ~/.a12s/team/
defaults:                             # applies to every agent computer (not Services); maps merge, lists replace
  harness: { kind: claude-code, version: 2.1.280, model: haiku }   # model: haiku | sonnet | opus | a full model id
  image: slim                         # slim | your image built FROM ghcr.io/coltonkirsten/a12s/slim:0.5.0
  credentials: [anthropic]            # names; values come from a12s.bindings.yaml (never committed)
  egress: { allow: [] }               # deny by default; the model API needs no entry (see below)
agent_computers:
  lead:
    instructions: |                   # its CLAUDE.md (claude-code) or AGENTS.md (codex)
      You are lead. …
    grants: { send: [worker1] }
  worker1:
    home: { preset: ./presets/worker }  # a directory of files for its home: CLAUDE.md, .claude/skills, .mcp.json
    grants: { send: [lead] }
```

`agent_computers:` was `computers:` before; `a12s up` still reads the old key for one release and prints a hint.

Agent computer fields (all optional except a harness, image and credential, which usually come from defaults):

- harness: {kind: claude-code, version: 2.1.280, model} or {kind: codex, version: 0.154.0} with credentials
  [openai]. Use these versions (published bundles); a version that has no bundle fails `a12s up`.
- image: `slim` or a custom image ref (see Custom images).
- instructions: text written to its home as CLAUDE.md (claude-code) or AGENTS.md (codex): its standing role.
- files: {path: text}: more text files for its home, by path relative to /home/agent (`.claude/skills/x/SKILL.md`,
  `.mcp.json`, `bin/tool`). A file that starts with `#!` is executable. Instructions plus files: at most 1 MiB.
- home: {preset: ./dir (relative to fleet.yaml), size: 10Gi}. `a12s up` reads the preset directory and sends it as
  files (UTF-8 text only; symlinks and binary files are refused). `instructions:` together with a preset that has a
  CLAUDE.md (AGENTS.md for codex) is an error: keep one. No instructions or files is fine: `hello: {}` with defaults
  works.
- credentials: [names]. anthropic → Claude Code, openai → Codex, github → GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN, any other name →
  file /run/a12s/secrets/<name> (the agent can read that file, but not list the directory: put the exact path in its
  instructions). A list on one agent computer REPLACES the defaults' list: with defaults [anthropic] write
  `credentials: [anthropic, stripe]`, not `[stripe]` (without anthropic every Turn fails "Not logged in"; the write
  warns). A credential with no value yet doesn't fail the write: it warns and the agent computer waits until it is set.
- egress: {allow: [hosts]}. HTTPS to those hosts only; plain http and private addresses are refused. The harness's
  own API and sign-in hosts are always added, so `allow: []` still lets Claude Code work. Allow everything public:
  `allow: ["*"]` (quote it: a bare * is YAML alias syntax and fails to parse).
- autonomy: full (default; Claude Code runs with bypassPermissions, the agent may run any command on its own
  computer) | restricted (every permission request is denied).
- grants: {send: [agent computers]}. uses: [services] (reach a Service's ports; an MCP port becomes a tool).
- resources: {cpu: 2, memory: 4Gi}. drives: [{name, at: /work/x, readOnly}] (top-level `drives: {x: {size: 20Gi,
  access: exclusive | shared | shared-write}}`).
- inbox: {maxMessages, maxBytes (≤1Mi), intro}. Bodies are at most 64 KiB.
- power: {sleepAfterIdle: 15m, wakeOnMessage: {from: [local, service:clock, computer:lead, token:web],
  maxWakesPerHour: 6}}. sleepAfterIdle is off or 1s to 7d (e.g. 5s, 15m, 2h, 1d); maxWakesPerHour 1-60. Default: never sleeps; once asleep, nothing wakes it unless its via is listed (no wildcard).
  A manual sleep (`a12s sleep`, SDK `sleep()`) is like sleepAfterIdle's: a listed sender's Message wakes it (with
  no wakeOnMessage it stays asleep until `wake`). `a12s sleep <c> --hold`, `sleep(hold=True)` or
  `sleep({ hold: true })` keeps it asleep until `wake`, ignoring wakeOnMessage (status says "auto-wake suppressed").
- security: {seccomp: ./profiles/x.json}: a Docker-format seccomp profile, relative to fleet.yaml, replacing
  Docker's default for that agent computer only; `a12s up` reads the file and sends the profile itself. From the SDK
  or the HTTP API, `seccomp` is the profile's JSON object. Set it only when the image's software needs blocked
  syscalls (Chromium's sandbox: see Custom images).

Top level also takes `services:` (see Services) and `drives:`. Change anything (instructions and preset files
included) and run `a12s up`: it applies at each agent computer's next idle moment, never mid-Turn, and keeps the
session. Changed files are written again; other files the agent made in its home stay.
fleet.lock pins `a12s: v0.5.0` and every image, bundle and Service digest; `a12s up` adds missing pins and never
moves one: to pick up a rebuilt image, give it a new tag.

`a12s up` makes the running Fleet match the file: it removes agent computers created from code and undoes changes
made through the SDK or API (GET /v1/fleet lists them as `drift`). When it would undo such changes it lists them and
asks `apply anyway? [y/N]`; without a terminal (CI) it fails unless `--force`. `a12s diff` shows what up would
change; `a12s export` writes the live Fleet back to the file instead (long instructions and files go to
presets/<name>/, seccomp profiles to profiles/<name>.json; comments in fleet.yaml are lost, so overwriting a file
that differs needs --force). Exporting onto your fleet.yaml makes the drift part of the file (up then undoes nothing);
to look first, export a copy: `cp -r . /tmp/copy && a12s -F /tmp/copy/fleet.yaml export --force`. Give each agent
computer one owner: the file or your code.

## What the agent sees

- Its instructions (CLAUDE.md, or AGENTS.md for codex) are its standing role. Put the role and protocol there, not
  in Message bodies: the agent treats bodies as untrusted data from the sender.
- Each Turn's prompt lists the delivered Messages, oldest first, each as
  `<msg-… n="1" id="m_…" from="<sender>" via="<via>" at="…">body</msg-…>`, so instructions can say "when a message
  via computer:coder arrives, …".
- With grants.send it has the tool `mcp__a12s__send`. It never waits for an answer: a reply arrives later as a new
  Message (via computer:<name>) in a new Turn. The session continues between Turns, so it remembers what it sent.
- Home is /home/agent (the home drive, kept across sleep and restarts). The root filesystem is read-only; the
  agent can install into its home (`pip install --user`, `npm install`, ~/bin) if egress allows the registry.

## CLI

```sh
a12s up                               # apply fleet.yaml (start the Controller if needed)
a12s up --force                       # also undo changes made through the API without asking (CI)
a12s up --memory-only-credentials     # a new Controller keeps credential values in memory only
a12s diff                             # fleet.yaml vs the live Fleet, changes nothing; exit 0 same, 2 differ, 1 failed
                                      #   (in make/set -e, exit 2 aborts: `a12s diff; test $$? -eq 2` expects drift)
a12s export [--force]                 # write the live Fleet back to fleet.yaml, presets/ and profiles/
a12s status                           # phase, inbox, power, warnings (--json for machines)
a12s send <c> "…" [--fresh] [--expires 60s] [--replace key] [--meta k=v]   # enqueue and exit; busy or asleep
a12s send <c> "…" --wait              # and stream the Turn that delivers it; exit 0 if it completed, 1 if not
a12s logs <c> [--follow]              # its journal, one "<seq> <type> <data JSON>" line per event, then exits;
                                      #   --follow keeps following (Ctrl-C). Types as in Words: turn.finished, …
a12s gateway [--web dir | --dev url | -- npm run dev] [--port 7012] [--allow status,events,send,inbox] [--computers c1,c2] [--no-open]
a12s ui [--port 7013] [--no-open]     # the web console (npx a12s-console; Node.js 20+); args go to the console
a12s inbox <c> [--bodies]             # pending Messages (human table; --json for machines)
a12s inbox hold <c> | inbox resume <c> | inbox rm <c> <id>   # hold delivery (Messages still queue), release, withdraw
a12s stop <c> | sleep <c> [--hold] | wake <c> [--clear-inbox]   # plain sleep: a sender listed in wakeOnMessage
                                      #   wakes it; --hold: no Message wakes it until wake
a12s shell <c|svc> [-- cmd…]          # audited terminal inside an agent computer or Service
a12s service ls | status <svc> | logs <svc> [-f] | login <svc>
a12s token create <name> --prefix biz- # <name> is a DNS label (bizapp), not the prefix. Owner powers on biz-* names,
                                      #   nothing outside. Prints the secret (a12st_…) once, alone on stdout:
                                      #   TOKEN=$(a12s token create bizapp --prefix biz-); with --json it is .secret
a12s token create <name> --actions send,events,status,inbox,power,stop --agent-computers c1,c2|'*'   # narrow
a12s creds set <name>                 # see Setup
a12s doctor                           # every check, with its fix
a12s down                             # stop all, keep disks;  down --purge deletes them (asks)
```

Every command finds the Fleet from -F path/fleet.yaml, $A12S_FLEET, or the nearest fleet.yaml upward. `<c>` is an
agent computer's name. Every command takes `--json` (before or after it) for scripts: `a12s status --json` is
{fleet, agentComputers: [{name, phase, inbox: {pending, held, …}, …}], …} (phase directly on each entry; held is
true/false, pending a number); `a12s --json send desk "hi" | jq -r .id` gives a Message id (m_ plus 26 capitals/digits);
`a12s inbox desk --json` is the inbox object below; `a12s --json token create bizapp --prefix biz- | jq -r .secret`.

## TypeScript SDK (npm install @coltonkirsten/a12s; Node 20+, ESM; in a browser through a bundler and the gateway)

```ts
const fleet = await Fleet.connect();
const hello = await fleet.agentComputers.create("hello", { instructions: "Be helpful" });
const reply = await hello.send("hi").wait();
await hello.remove();
```

```ts
import { Fleet, A12sError, NotFound } from "@coltonkirsten/a12s";
const fleet = await Fleet.connect();  // nearest fleet.yaml's Fleet, else the only running one, as owner (no token);
                                      // or Fleet.connect({ fleet }), Fleet.connect({ url, token }), env A12S_URL +
                                      // A12S_TOKEN; in a page served by the gateway: same origin, no arguments.
                                      // Fleet.connect({ token }): this machine's Fleet, found the same way, under
                                      // another token (e.g. a prefix token's secret) instead of the owner's

// create takes any agent computer field (as in fleet.yaml); the rest comes from defaults. Resolves once it is up.
const coder = await fleet.agentComputers.create("coder", {
  instructions: "You write and run Python.", egress: { allow: ["pypi.org", "files.pythonhosted.org"] },
});                                   // a taken name: A12sError code "exists"; { replace: true } overwrites it
const lead = await fleet.agentComputers.get("lead");   // throws NotFound if there is none; also list()
lead.name; lead.spec; lead.effective; lead.status.phase  // as written, with defaults merged, status: a snapshot
await lead.reload();                                     // refreshes the snapshot

const m = await lead.send("…");                     // or send("…", { sender, metadata, fresh, expires (seconds),
m.id; m.state;                                      //   replaceKey, idempotencyKey }); returns at once

// Send and wait for the answer; onEvent streams that Turn's events as they happen:
const r = await lead.send("Explain TCP in two sentences.").wait({
  onEvent: (ev) => { if (ev.type === "text.delta") process.stdout.write(ev.data.text); },
});                                   // wait({ signal }) too; m.wait() works on a sent Message, even after its Turn ended
r.status; r.text; r.id; r.error; r.messages; r.tools; r.message.id   // a Turn plus the Message it delivered

const turns = fleet.turns(["lead", "worker1"]);     // Turns as they end; no argument = every agent computer
await turns.ready();                                // connected: nothing after this is missed
for await (const t of turns) { t.agentComputer; t.text; t.status; t.tokens?.output; t.messages[0]?.via; break; }

const evs = lead.events();                          // live from now; fleet.events(names?) for several or all
await evs.ready();
for await (const ev of evs) { if (ev.type === "text.delta") ev.data.text; }   // typed by ev.type
lead.events({ turn: r.id });                        // replay one Turn from its start; ends after its turn.finished
const past = await lead.turns({ limit: 20 });       // its last finished Turns (an array), newest first

await lead.update({ instructions: "…", power: null }); // JSON merge patch: null goes back to the default;
                                                       // a busy one picks it up at its next idle moment
const box = await lead.inbox({ bodies: true });     // {computer, held, holdReason?, pending, claimed, messages:
                                                    //   [{id, seq, state, sender, via, body?, replaceKey?, …}], …}
await lead.message(m.id); await lead.withdraw(m.id); // withdraw: a pending Message is removed, never delivered
await lead.hold({ reason: "triage" }); await lead.resume();   // hold delivery (sends still queue); release it
await lead.stop(); await lead.wake();               // wake({ clearInbox: true }) discards pending Messages first
await lead.sleep();                                 // asleep, and a sender listed in wakeOnMessage wakes it
await lead.sleep({ hold: true });                   // asleep until wake(): NO Message wakes it, wakeOnMessage or not
await coder.remove();                               // stops and removes it; its drives are kept
await fleet.status();                               // every agent computer and Service: phase, inbox, power

const clock = await fleet.services.get("clock");    // fleet.services: create, get, list
await clock.sleep(); await clock.wake();            // Service: reload, update, sleep, wake, remove
const app = await fleet.tokens.create("bizapp", { prefix: "biz-" });  // owner only; app.secret shown once
const tok = await fleet.tokens.create("web", { actions: ["send", "status"], agentComputers: ["lead"] });
tok.secret;                                         // fleet.tokens.list(), remove(name)

const { version, spec, drift } = await fleet.get(); // the whole Fleet as written (FleetSpec)
await fleet.credentials.set("stripe", key);         // agent computers using it get it at once; values never read back
await fleet.credentials.list();                     // [{name, set, usedBy}]; remove(name): 409 in_use while used
await fleet.replace((f) => { f.defaults!.power = { sleepAfterIdle: "15m" }; });  // If-Match, retried on conflict
// errors: A12sError {status, code, message, fix}, NotFound (a 404, subclass of A12sError); streams:
// A12sStreamError, A12sGapError (onGap: "throw"). A failed Turn is not an error: wait() returns it, status "failed".
// A write's warnings (a grant to a missing agent computer, a missing harness credential) go to console.warn.
```

events() and turns() start live (nothing from before they connect), and every events() and turns() of one Fleet
share one connection (GET /v1/events), however many agent computers they watch. Types: Turn {agentComputer, id,
session, status, text (everything the agent said in the Turn, concatenated), error?, messages: [{id, sender, via}],
tools: [{id, name, input, output, isError}], usage, tokens?, startedAt?, finishedAt}. tool input/output and usage are `unknown`: cast,
e.g. `(t.tools[0].input as { body: string }).body`. Streams end with `break` or `.close()`; both also take
`{ signal }`. The spec types are `AgentComputerSpec` and `FleetSpec`. `connect()` and `A12sClient` (name-first calls
such as `a12s.send("hello", "…")`) still work for one release, deprecated.

## Python SDK (pip install a12s; Python 3.10+)

```python
fleet = a12s.Fleet()            # connects to the running fleet (or url=, token=)
hello = fleet.agent_computers.create("hello", instructions="Be helpful")
reply = hello.send("hi").wait()
hello.remove()
```

```python
import a12s
fleet = a12s.Fleet()                  # same discovery; a12s.Fleet(fleet="team"), a12s.Fleet(url=…, token=…);
                                      # a12s.Fleet(token=secret): this machine's Fleet under another token
coder = fleet.agent_computers.create("coder", instructions="You write and run Python.",
                                     egress={"allow": ["pypi.org"]}, power={"sleepAfterIdle": "30m"})
# keyword arguments are agent computer fields; nested keys camelCase as in fleet.yaml; replace=True overwrites
lead = fleet.agent_computers.get("lead")   # raises a12s.NotFound; fleet.agent_computers.list()
lead.name, lead.spec, lead.effective, lead.status.phase   # a snapshot; lead.reload() refreshes it
m = lead.send("…", sender="app", metadata={"k": "v"}, fresh=False, expires=None, replace_key=None)
m.id, m.state                         # body is a str; options are keyword-only; returns at once
r = lead.send("…").wait(on_event=lambda ev: ev.type == "text.delta" and print(ev.data["text"], end="", flush=True))
r.text, r.status, r.id, r.error, r.messages, r.tools, r.message.id   # m.wait() works later too, even after the Turn
with fleet.turns(["lead", "worker1"]) as turns:   # entering waits until connected
    lead.send("task")
    for t in turns:                   # t.agent_computer, t.text, t.status, t.error, t.tokens, t.messages[0].via
        for tool in t.tools:          # tool.name, tool.input (dict), tool.output, tool.is_error
            pass
        break
for ev in lead.events():              # ev.type, ev.agent_computer, ev.turn, ev.data (dict, camelCase keys)
    pass                              # lead.events(turn=r.id) replays one Turn; fleet.events() has them all
lead.turns(limit=20)                  # a list of its last finished Turns, newest first (without limit: live, as they
                                      # end); on AsyncFleet: past = await lead.turns(limit=20)
lead.update(instructions="…")         # changes only these fields; applies at its next idle moment
box = lead.inbox(bodies=True)         # box.held, box.pending, box.messages[i].id/.body/.state/.via
lead.message(m.id); lead.withdraw(m.id)   # withdraw: a pending Message is removed, never delivered
lead.hold(reason="triage"); lead.resume() # hold delivery (sends still queue); release it
lead.stop(); lead.wake()                  # wake(clear_inbox=True) discards pending Messages first
lead.sleep()                              # asleep, and a sender listed in wakeOnMessage wakes it
lead.sleep(hold=True)                     # asleep until wake(): NO Message wakes it, wakeOnMessage or not
coder.remove()                        # stops and removes it; its drives are kept
fleet.status().agent_computers        # every agent computer: phase, inbox, power
fleet.services.get("clock").sleep()   # Service: reload, update, sleep, wake, remove
app = fleet.tokens.create("bizapp", prefix="biz-")   # owner only; app.secret once
tok = fleet.tokens.create("web", actions=["send", "status"], agent_computers=["lead"])   # tok.secret once
state = fleet.get()                   # a FleetState (attributes, not a dict): .version, .spec (FleetSpec, a dict),
                                      # .drift (list of Change: op, kind, name, fields); there is no fleet.reload()
fleet.credentials.set("stripe", key)  # agent computers using it get it at once; values are never read back
fleet.credentials.list()              # [CredentialInfo(name, set, used_by)]; remove(name) raises in_use while used
fleet.replace(lambda f: f.defaults.update(power={"sleepAfterIdle": "15m"}))   # If-Match, retried on conflict
fleet.close()                         # or: with a12s.Fleet() as fleet:
# async: fleet = a12s.AsyncFleet(); the same objects with await / async for / async with:
# r = await lead.send("…").wait(), or m = await lead.send("…") then r = await m.wait(). Close it with
# `await fleet.aclose()` (AsyncFleet has no close()), or use `async with a12s.AsyncFleet() as fleet:`
# errors: a12s.A12sError (status, code, fix; a12s.NotFound is one), a12s.A12sStreamError, a12s.A12sGapError;
# a failed Turn is returned with status "failed", not raised. A write's warnings arrive as warnings.warn(A12sWarning).
# lead.events(turn=r.id) replays one Turn and ends after its turn.finished
```

Iteration blocks until the next Turn or event; it has no timeout. To bound it, run it in a thread or use
AsyncFleet with asyncio.wait_for. `a12s.connect()` and `Client` (name-first calls such as
`client.send("hello", "…")`) still work for one release, deprecated.

## Recipe: hand work from one agent to another

```yaml
# fleet.yaml, with defaults as in the fleet.yaml section
agent_computers:
  lead:
    grants: { send: [worker1] }
    instructions: |
      # You are lead
      You coordinate `worker1` with your `send` tool (mcp__a12s__send). You never do the work yourself.
      When a task arrives (a message not via computer:worker1):
      1. `send` the work to worker1, asking for a short answer sent back to `lead`.
      2. Reply `DISPATCHED` and end your turn. Don't wait: the result arrives as a new message.
      When worker1's result arrives (via="computer:worker1"): reply `FINAL ANSWER:` followed by the answer.
  worker1:
    grants: { send: [lead] }
    instructions: |
      # You are worker1
      `lead` sends you work (via="computer:lead"). Do it, then `send` the result to `lead` starting with
      `RESULT:`. Then reply `SENT`.
```

```python
# app.py: python app.py "task"
import sys, a12s
fleet = a12s.Fleet()
lead = fleet.agent_computers.get("lead")
with fleet.turns(["lead", "worker1"]) as turns:       # watch first: the answer comes in a later Turn of lead
    lead.send(sys.argv[1], fresh=True)                # fresh: a new conversation per task
    for t in turns:
        if t.status != "completed":
            sys.exit(f"{t.computer} {t.status}: {t.error}")
        if t.computer == "lead" and "FINAL ANSWER:" in t.text:
            print(t.text.split("FINAL ANSWER:", 1)[1].strip())
            break
```

A worker's result is in its send call (`t.tools`, name `mcp__a12s__send`, input `{computer, body}`), not in t.text.
The receiver's Turn can finish before the sender's (a send happens mid-Turn), so match Turns by agent computer and
content, never by arrival order.
Without fresh, lead remembers earlier tasks and may repeat an old answer. To make the pair from code instead, create
them one after the other: a grant may name an agent computer that doesn't exist yet (the write warns).

## Custom images

Add tools (a toolchain, a CLI, a browser) by building FROM the slim image of your a12s release. slim is
node:24-bookworm-slim (Debian, apt) plus git, ripgrep, python3, curl, ca-certificates and computerd.

```dockerfile
# images/agent/Dockerfile
FROM ghcr.io/coltonkirsten/a12s/slim:0.5.0
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends jq ffmpeg && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
```

```sh
docker build -t my-agent:1 images/agent      # a local tag works; a12s up pulls only images it doesn't have
```

```yaml
agent_computers:
  worker: { image: my-agent:1 }
```

- The tag is the release without the v (slim:0.5.0). Admission needs the `ai.a12s.computerd.version` label FROM
  slim sets (same minor as the CLI) and computerd at /opt/a12s/computerd/dist/main.js; don't remove either.
- The Dockerfile runs as root; don't set USER, ENTRYPOINT or CMD (a12s ignores them: computerd starts as root and
  runs the agent as uid 1000 with /home mounted over). Install system-wide (/usr, /opt), not into /home/agent.
- To change the image, build a new tag and change it in fleet.yaml; a pinned tag keeps its old digest.
- A browser: install Chromium (and Playwright) in the image and give that agent computer
  `security: { seccomp: ./profiles/chromium.json }` (Docker's default profile plus clone/unshare with
  CLONE_NEWUSER, setns, chroot). Never use --no-sandbox. Full Dockerfile and profile:
  https://github.com/coltonkirsten/a12s-cookbook/tree/main/examples/browser-agent

## Services

A Service is an image a12s runs next to the agent computers. It may only do what its grants say: `grants.send` lets
it enqueue Messages (they arrive via service:<name>), `uses` lets agent computers reach its ports.

```yaml
services:                             # top level, next to agent_computers:
  clock:
    image: my-clock:1                 # an image you built; it must contain /a12s/service.json
    grants: { send: [worker] }
    config: { to: worker, every: 2m } # becomes /run/a12s/config/config.json
    # env: {K: v}, credentials: [name], publish: ["127.0.0.1:8787:8080"], egress: {allow: [...]}, uses: [svc]
agent_computers:
  worker:
    power: { sleepAfterIdle: 30m, wakeOnMessage: { from: [service:clock] } }   # only if it may sleep
```

A clock in Go with svckit (package `github.com/coltonkirsten/a12s/services/svckit`, standard library only, inside
the a12s module; needs Go 1.26):

```sh
mkdir clock && cd clock && go mod init example.com/clock
go get github.com/coltonkirsten/a12s/services/svckit@v0.5.0
```

svckit is a package inside the module github.com/coltonkirsten/a12s (there is no separate svckit module or tag): go get
writes `require github.com/coltonkirsten/a12s v0.5.0` to go.mod and fills go.sum. Don't hand-write either; run
`go mod tidy` after writing main.go. The Dockerfile below copies both, so a build script runs, in this order:
`(cd clock && go mod tidy) && docker build -t my-clock:1 clock`.

```go
// main.go
package main

import (
	"log"
	"net/http"
	"time"

	"github.com/coltonkirsten/a12s/services/svckit"
)

type config struct {
	To    string `json:"to"`
	Every string `json:"every"`
}

func main() {
	var cfg config
	if err := svckit.LoadConfig(&cfg); err != nil { // reads /run/a12s/config/config.json
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	every, err := svckit.ParseDuration(cfg.Every) // 0, 90s, 15m, 1h, 7d
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	c, err := svckit.NewClient() // mTLS client from A12S_API and /run/a12s/tls
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	mux := http.NewServeMux()
	svckit.Health(mux) // GET /healthz
	go http.ListenAndServe(":8080", mux)
	for range time.Tick(every) {
		msg, status, err := c.Send(cfg.To, svckit.Enqueue{Body: "tick: run date and say hello", Sender: "clock", ReplaceKey: "tick"})
		if err != nil {
			log.Printf("send: %d %v", status, err) // *svckit.APIError {Status, Code, Message, Fix}; 403 no_grant names the grant
			continue
		}
		log.Printf("sent %s (%s)", msg.ID, msg.State)
	}
}
```

svckit.Enqueue fields: Body, Sender, Metadata map[string]string, Fresh bool, IdempotencyKey, Expires *int64
(seconds), ReplaceKey. Also svckit.Secret(name) ([]byte, error) reads /run/a12s/secrets/<name>, and
c.Get(computer, id) (svckit.Message, error) reads back its own Message {ID, Seq, State, ExpiresAt, Replaced}.

```json
{ "a12s": 1, "name": "clock", "version": "1.0.0", "user": 1000,
  "health": { "http": { "port": 8080, "path": "/healthz" } } }
```

```dockerfile
# Dockerfile, next to main.go, go.mod, go.sum and service.json
FROM golang:1.26 AS build
WORKDIR /src
COPY go.mod go.sum ./
RUN go mod download
COPY . .
RUN CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -trimpath -o /out/clock .

FROM alpine:3
COPY --from=build /out/clock /usr/local/bin/clock
COPY service.json /a12s/service.json
USER 1000:1000
CMD ["/usr/local/bin/clock"]
```

```sh
docker build -t my-clock:1 clock && a12s up && a12s service logs clock -f
```

- service.json (the manifest) is required: in the image at /a12s/service.json, or inline under
  services.<name>.manifest. `user` is a non-zero uid (match the image's USER). Optional: `ports`
  ({"api": {"port": 8080, "protocol": "http"}}, add "mcp": {"path": "/mcp"} to expose an MCP server to agent
  computers that `uses:` it), `credentials` ([{"name": "x", "required": false}]), `state` ({"at": "/var/lib/svc", "size": "1Gi"}),
  `tmpfs`, `resources`, `login` ({command, produces}, run by `a12s service login <svc>`).
- The process runs as that uid, read-only root filesystem, no capabilities; write to `state.at` or a `tmpfs` path.
  Reaches the internet only through its own `egress.allow`. A Service that exits is restarted with backoff.
- Any language works: read config.json, call POST $A12S_API/v1/agent-computers/{c}/inbox with the client
  certificate in /run/a12s/tls/{ca.crt,cert.pem,key.pem}.
- No Service needed for a plain schedule: host cron running `a12s -F ~/proj/fleet.yaml send lead "…" --replace daily`.

## Browser (gateway)

`a12s gateway` serves your app and, on the same origin, the API at /v1/ under a scoped token the page never sees.
The page imports the npm package through a bundler (Vite here); that is the only way in. Run it in the Fleet's
directory (or -F path/fleet.yaml).

```sh
a12s gateway                          # built-in dashboard: every agent computer, live events, a send box
a12s gateway -- npx vite              # your dev server behind it (or -- npm run dev: Next.js, …), hot reload included
a12s gateway --dev http://localhost:5173   # a dev server that is already running
a12s gateway --web dist               # your built app (npx vite build writes dist/)
```

It prints and opens http://127.0.0.1:7012/?key=… (new key each run; `--no-open` only prints). Open that link, not
the dev server's own port: the key becomes a cookie that /v1/ needs. Scripts and tests use the key as a
token: Fleet.connect({ url: "http://127.0.0.1:7012", token: key }). The page may use status, events, send and
inbox on every agent computer, not create or change them; narrow with `--allow status,events` and `--computers worker`. Messages from the page arrive
via token:gateway-7012. Loopback only; to serve other people, run your own server with login that calls a12s with a
scoped token: narrow (`a12s token create web --actions send,status --agent-computers lead`) or, if it creates
agent computers, a prefix token (`--prefix web-`).

A page with live events of worker and a send box: `npm install @coltonkirsten/a12s vite`, these two files, then
`a12s gateway -- npx vite`. No Vite or dev-server config is needed: the gateway runs the command, waits for the
http://localhost:<port> URL it prints (or `--dev-port <port>`), and proxies it.

```html
<!-- index.html -->
<!doctype html>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<form id="f"><input id="msg" size="60"><button>Send</button></form>
<pre id="log"></pre>
<script type="module" src="/main.js"></script>
```

```js
// main.js
import { Fleet } from "@coltonkirsten/a12s";
const fleet = await Fleet.connect();
const worker = await fleet.agentComputers.get("worker");
const log = (s) => (document.getElementById("log").textContent += s + "\n");
document.getElementById("f").onsubmit = async (e) => {
  e.preventDefault();
  await worker.send(document.getElementById("msg").value);
};
for await (const ev of worker.events()) {
  if (ev.type === "text.delta") log(ev.data.text);
  if (ev.type === "tool.started") log(`→ ${ev.data.name}`);
  if (ev.type === "turn.finished") log(`turn ${ev.data.status} ${ev.data.error ?? ""}`);
}
```

## HTTP API (any language)

Base http://127.0.0.1:<port>, header Authorization: Bearer <token>, both from ~/.a12s/<fleet>/controller.json
({"port", "token"}). Errors are {code, message, fix}.

- Messages: POST /v1/agent-computers/{c}/inbox {"body", "idempotencyKey", "sender"?, "metadata"?, "fresh"?,
  "expires"? (seconds), "replaceKey"?} → {id, state, …}; GET /v1/status.
- Events: GET /v1/events is one SSE stream for the whole Fleet (?agentComputers=a,b filters): id is an opaque
  string, Last-Event-ID resumes, `event: head` marks live, `event: gap` = events lost (resync). It also carries
  fleet.changed, agent_computer.phase, inbox.changed and service.phase. GET /v1/agent-computers/{c}/events is one agent computer's journal (id =
  seq; ?turn=<id> replays one Turn and then stays open: stop reading at its turn.finished).
  GET /v1/agent-computers/{c}/turns?limit=20 → {turns: [Turn]}, newest first.
- One agent computer (owner or prefix token): PUT /v1/agent-computers/{c} with its spec as JSON (fleet.yaml's
  fields; seccomp is the profile object) creates or replaces it; add `If-None-Match: *` to only create (409 exists
  if taken). PATCH is a JSON merge patch (null removes a key, so it falls back to the default); DELETE removes it, drives kept.
  GET /v1/agent-computers/{c} → {name, spec, effective, status}; GET /v1/agent-computers lists them. The same
  PUT/PATCH/DELETE exist on /v1/services/{s}. These writes change only that one; last write wins.
- The whole Fleet: GET /v1/fleet → {version, fleet, drift} with ETag "<version>". PUT /v1/fleet {"fleet": …} with
  If-Match: "<version>" replaces it, or answers 412 version_mismatch if it changed since you read it.
- A write on one agent computer also answers `agentComputer: {name, spec, effective, status}` (a Service write:
  `service`), e.g. `curl … -X PATCH … | jq .agentComputer.spec.instructions`. POST …/inbox needs only "body".
- Every write takes ?dryRun=true (check it exactly as the write would, list the changes, change nothing) and answers {version, changes: [{op:
  create|update|remove, kind: agentComputer|service, name, when: now|idle, fields?, diff?: [{path, before?, after?}]}],
  warnings, errors, …}; diff lists each changed leaf of an update (path "grants.send"; lists and values are leaves). A
  missing harness or image (in the spec and in defaults) is 400 missing_field; a credential with no value is a warning,
  and the agent computer or Service waits for it.
- Credentials (owner or prefix token): GET /v1/credentials → {credentials: [{name, set, usedBy, updatedAt?}]} (names, never
  values); PUT /v1/credentials/{name} {"value": "…"} stores it and updates the agent computers and Services using it
  (starting the ones that waited for it);
  DELETE /v1/credentials/{name} is 409 in_use while one uses it, 404 if none is stored.
- Tokens (owner token): POST /v1/tokens {"name", "prefix"} or {"name", "actions", "computers"} → {name, …, secret}
  (secret shown once); GET /v1/tokens (each with createdAt and lastUsedAt?, recorded at most once a minute); DELETE /v1/tokens/{name}.
- A prefix token may do everything the owner can on agent computers, Services and credentials whose names start with
  its prefix (create/get/update/remove, send, inbox, events, power, stop, shell, Service logs and login). Their
  grants.send, uses and drives, defaults included, must be inside the prefix too (a default grant outside: override
  it with the agent computer's own grants); its specs may name any credential. Reads list only names inside it.
  Anything outside is 403 out_of_prefix; /v1/fleet (so defaults), /v1/apply, drives and tokens are 403 forbidden.
  Egress, image, seccomp and resources are its call: trust it like the owner for its agent computers.
- The old /v1/computers/... paths still work for one release.
- Error codes (`code`, stable): invalid, missing_field, bad_metadata, bad_expires (400);
  unauthorized (401); forbidden, no_grant, out_of_prefix (403); not_found, unknown_request (404); busy, conflict,
  exists, in_use, idempotency_conflict, not_idle, attached (409); gone (410); version_mismatch (412);
  body_too_large, exceeds_inbox (413); inbox_full (429); asleep (503).

## API surface

<!-- api-surface: generated by `go test ./internal/controller -run TestLLMsTxtSurface -update`; do not edit -->
Routes, with the action a narrow token needs (owner: the owner token only; prefix: a prefix token, for names inside it). A prefix token may also make every action route on names inside its prefix.

```text
GET /v1/fleet                                   owner
PUT /v1/fleet                                   owner
GET /v1/status                                  status
GET /v1/agent-computers                         status
GET /v1/agent-computers/{c}                     status
PUT /v1/agent-computers/{c}                     owner, or prefix
PATCH /v1/agent-computers/{c}                   owner, or prefix
DELETE /v1/agent-computers/{c}                  owner, or prefix
GET /v1/events                                  events
GET /v1/agent-computers/{c}/events              events
GET /v1/agent-computers/{c}/turns               events
POST /v1/agent-computers/{c}/turns/{id}/stop    stop
POST /v1/agent-computers/{c}/power              power
POST /v1/apply                                  owner
POST /v1/agent-computers/{c}/shell              owner, or prefix
GET /v1/drives                                  owner
DELETE /v1/drives/{d}                           owner
POST /v1/agent-computers/{c}/inbox              send
GET /v1/agent-computers/{c}/inbox               inbox
GET /v1/agent-computers/{c}/inbox/{id}          send or inbox
GET /v1/agent-computers/{c}/inbox/{id}/events   send or inbox
DELETE /v1/agent-computers/{c}/inbox/{id}       send or inbox
POST /v1/agent-computers/{c}/inbox/clear        inbox
POST /v1/agent-computers/{c}/inbox/hold         inbox
POST /v1/agent-computers/{c}/inbox/resume       inbox
GET /v1/services                                status
GET /v1/services/{s}                            status
PUT /v1/services/{s}                            owner, or prefix
PATCH /v1/services/{s}                          owner, or prefix
DELETE /v1/services/{s}                         owner, or prefix
GET /v1/services/{s}/logs                       owner, or prefix
POST /v1/services/{s}/power                     owner, or prefix
POST /v1/services/{s}/shell                     owner, or prefix
POST /v1/services/{s}/login                     owner, or prefix
DELETE /v1/services/{s}/login                   owner, or prefix
GET /v1/credentials                             owner, or prefix
PUT /v1/credentials/{name}                      owner, or prefix
DELETE /v1/credentials/{name}                   owner, or prefix
POST /v1/tokens                                 owner
GET /v1/tokens                                  owner
DELETE /v1/tokens/{name}                        owner
```

SDK objects (Python names; TypeScript is camelCase):

- Fleet: TypeScript get, replace, events, turns, status; Python close, status, events, turns, get, replace; Python AsyncFleet aclose, status, events, turns, get, replace
- AgentComputers: TypeScript create, get, list; Python create, get, list
- AgentComputer: TypeScript reload, update, remove, send, events, turns, sleep, wake, hold, resume, stop, inbox, message, withdraw; Python reload, send, events, turns, update, sleep, wake, hold, resume, stop, inbox, message, withdraw, remove
- Services: TypeScript create, get, list; Python create, get, list
- Service: TypeScript reload, update, remove, sleep, wake; Python reload, update, sleep, wake, remove
- Tokens: TypeScript create, list, remove; Python create, list, remove
- Credentials: TypeScript set, list, remove; Python set, list, remove

Deprecated one release (name-first): TypeScript A12sClient status, computer, send, prompt, events, turns, inbox, message, withdraw, stop, sleep, wake, hold, resume, services, service, createToken, putFleet; Python Client close, status, computer, send, prompt, events, turns, inbox, message, withdraw, stop, sleep, wake, hold, resume, services, service, create_token, put_fleet
<!-- /api-surface -->

## Patterns and gotchas

- For the Turn that delivers your own Message, use `send(...).wait()`: it can't miss it, however late you call it.
  To follow Turns your Message causes on OTHER agent computers (lead's final answer in the hand-off recipe comes in
  a later Turn), open `fleet.turns()` first (`await turns.ready()` / `with fleet.turns(...)`), then send.
- A plain `sleep()` / `a12s sleep <c>` leaves wakeOnMessage in charge: a Message from a listed sender wakes it (so
  you can test wakeOnMessage by sleeping it and sending). To keep it asleep until `wake()` whatever is sent, use
  `sleep(hold=True)` (Python), `sleep({ hold: true })` (TypeScript) or `a12s sleep <c> --hold`.
  After a send, reload() and check `status.phase` until it is Busy or Ready; an old Ready event proves nothing.
- A seccomp profile's archMap/architectures take libseccomp names only (SCMP_ARCH_X86_64, SCMP_ARCH_X86,
  SCMP_ARCH_X32, SCMP_ARCH_AARCH64, SCMP_ARCH_ARM, …); the simplest valid profile that runs everything is
  `{"defaultAction": "SCMP_ACT_ALLOW"}` (a12s warns that it allows every syscall).
- Agent computers made from code are for work that comes and goes (one per task, user or branch): create,
  send(...).wait(), remove. Keep long-lived roles in fleet.yaml; `a12s up` removes what the file doesn't list.
- `spec`, `effective` and `status` on an AgentComputer are a snapshot: `reload()` before reading the phase again.
- Two programs editing the same agent computer: the last write wins. Whole-Fleet edits go through `fleet.replace`,
  which retries on 412 version_mismatch.
- Send each new task with fresh=true so the agent starts a new conversation.
- An agent can only `send` to agent computers in its grants.send; anything else gets 403 no_grant.
- Every Claude Code Turn logs one or two `egress.denied` events for telemetry hosts: harmless.
- Nothing is delivered? `a12s inbox <c>` (held? says why; `a12s inbox resume <c>`), `a12s status` (asleep?
  `a12s wake <c>`), `a12s doctor`. A Turn failing with "Failed to authenticate": fix the credential, `a12s up`.
- After Docker or the Controller restarts, the Controller resumes the Fleet with the credentials it stored. With
  --memory-only-credentials it holds none until you run `a12s up` again.
- Upgrading a12s: change `a12s:` in fleet.lock to the new version, delete its `slim` pin, rebuild custom images FROM
  the new slim under new tags, `a12s up`.

  (concepts, recipes, sdk, api, fleet-file, cli, inbox and power, services, credentials, images, security)
- Changing a12s itself: CONTRIBUTING.md and AGENTS.md in the repo
